ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circular roundabout, with an empty circle in the center, and four roads connected to the outside of the roundabout, located respectively in the four directions upper left, upper right, lower right, and lower left; beside each road there is one car entering the roundabout. The arrows on the roundabout show that the vehicles travel in the clockwise direction. There are altogether four entrance/exit positions in the figure. Then reason: Label the four entrances/exits as 1, 2, 3, 4 in clockwise order, and also label the car entering from the i-th entrance/exit as car i. Because each car must leave before going around one full circle, car i cannot leave from the i-th exit from which it entered, and can only choose the other three exits. Also because no two cars leave from the same exit, this is assigning 4 cars one-to-one to 4 exits, and not allowing any car to be assigned to its own exit, that is, calculating the number of derangements of 4 elements. Count by inclusion-exclusion: All one-to-one assignments have 4! = 24 cases. Subtract the cases where at least one car leaves from its own exit: 4! - C(4,1)3! + C(4,2)2! - C(4,3)1! + C(4,4)0! = 24 - 24 + 12 - 4 + 1 = 9. Therefore there are altogether 9 different ways.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows a roundabout with exactly four entry/exit roads, one car entering from each road, and arrows indicating clockwise motion. Label the four junctions/exits 1, 2, 3, 4 in clockwise order, and label each car by the junction where it enters. Since each car must leave before completing a full circuit, car i may leave by any exit except exit i. Since no two cars leave by the same exit, the choices form a permutation of the four exits with no fixed point. Count these by inclusion-exclusion: start with all 4! one-to-one assignments of cars to exits, subtract assignments where at least one car uses its own exit. The count is 4! - C(4,1)3! + C(4,2)2! - C(4,3)1! + C(4,4)0! = 24 - 24 + 12 - 4 + 1 = 9.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: there are four access points around the circular roundabout, and the cars move clockwise around the circle. Label the four entry/exit points A, B, C, D clockwise, and label each car by its entry point. The text condition that a car leaves before making a complete circuit means no car can leave at its own labeled point; the condition that no two cars share an exit means the exit assignment is a fixed-point-free permutation of A, B, C, D. Count such permutations by cycle type instead of inclusion-exclusion. With four labels and no fixed points, the permutation must be either two disjoint 2-cycles or one 4-cycle. Therefore the total number of possible leaving patterns is 3 + 6 = 9.
